source.note: Captures the AI SDK inbound request conversion: an aisdk Request{Model:'gpt-4', Messages:[{Role:'system', Parts:[{Type:'text', Text:'System message'}]}]} fed to convertToLLMRequest must yield an llm.Request with one Message{Role:'system', Content.Content:'System message'}. The Go test asserts result.Messages[0] equals the expected llm.Message via assert.Equal. This is a request-conversion contract case: inbound_http carries the raw aisdk Request body (the test builds the struct directly, not an HTTP body — body_json below is the equivalent JSON serialization), unified_request carries the converted llm.Request. selected_channel, outbound_http, upstream_http and client_http are null because convertToLLMRequest does not exercise those stages.

inbound_http._comment: Equivalent JSON serialization of the aisdk.Request struct the Go test constructs inline. The Go test calls convertToLLMRequest(req) directly (no HTTP layer), so method/url/headers are not asserted; body_json shows the equivalent wire-shape of the input struct.

unified_request._comment: Asserted by TestConvertToLLMRequestComprehensive_SystemMessage subtest 'simple system message'. The Go test uses assert.Equal(t, expected, result.Messages[0]) where expected is llm.Message{Role:'system', Content:{Content: lo.ToPtr('System message')}}. Model is preserved from the input ('gpt-4').
